title: POC Weekly Sync - Rollout & Go-live Planning

Agreed next steps: Redwood to share canary runbook and playbook, customer to provide traffic split targets and compliance checklist by next week.

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-07 15:00 PDT | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Elena (BrightCart Head of Platform), Samir (CTO), Dana (Privacy), Josh (SRE)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick agenda — finalize the canary plan, cutover steps, monitoring and runbooks. is that good?
[00:14] Elena: yep that works, we want to make sure the first canary is tightly scoped, low blast radius. also need to see what the rollback looks like.
[00:28] Carlos: ok, i'll start with what we tested last week — we ran two variants on Redwood Dedicated, small GPU pool, and we captured p50/p95/p99 — p95 was about 420ms for the 512 token gen and p99 dipped to ~1.2s under burst. there was a little jitter when kv cache warmed, so we recommend warmup traffic.
[00:48] Josh: when you say kv cache warmed, do you mean prefix caching? we've seen weird cold-starts with our current infra that spike p99.
[00:56] Carlos: yeah prefix/KV cache, sometimes transcribed as K V cache in the logs, but basically the KV state for chat sessions. warming with small ramp helps.
[01:08] Samir: are those numbers from the hosted API or Dedicated? we need to know because our SLA targets are different on dedicated capacity.
[01:15] Carlos: Dedicated pool — same config we'll use in the pilot. on hosted we saw similar median but different tail.
[01:23] Maya: ok, so for canary planning — proposal: phase 1 internal canary (0.5-1% of traffic), phase 2 external canary 5-10% with A/B evaluation for quality regression, phase 3 ramp to 30% then full cutover. each phase has a 24-48h hold window and clear rollback gates. thoughts?
[01:44] Elena: that seems sensible. what's your suggested quality metric for A/B? we don't want to surface worse completions to users.
[01:52] Carlos: recommend using the eval set we ran — we have BLEU-style and also custom business metrics like false-action rate, hallucination flags, and latency SLO. A/B will compare these plus manual spot checks.
[02:06] Dana: on the compliance side we need audit logs for every inference, redaction rules, and KMS integration. does Dedicated support customer-managed keys?
[02:16] Maya: yes — Redwood Private/Dedicated can integrate with customer KMS; we support HSM-backed keys for on-prem or VPC deployments. we'll send the KMS doc.
[02:26] Dana: perfect — also need to ensure SSO/SAML assertions are captured for admin actions.
[02:32] Priya: noted, i'll include the SSO checklist in the handoff doc.
[02:38] Josh: for monitoring — what are the core SLIs we should wire into our dashboards? latency p95, p99, error rate, token generation throttles?
[02:47] Carlos: yes p95/p99, error rate by model and route, backpressure signals from the runtime, queue length, and KV cache miss rate. also model-level quality regressions via eval harness. we can push metrics to Prometheus and provide Grafana dashboards.
[03:03] Samir: do you provide out-of-the-box runbooks for rollbacks? our SREs prefer step-by-step.
[03:10] Maya: we have a canary runbook template — includes traffic switch commands, rollback criteria, script snippets for k8s, and playbook for warmup. i'll attach a draft after the call.
[03:19] Elena: want to see example manifests — like how you pin model versions and set autoscale policies.
[03:26] Carlos: we'll include sample manifests. note: autoscale is based on token throughput and GPU utilization; for the pilot we recommend a conservative min replicas to avoid cold starts.
[03:38] Josh: what's the recommended timeout and retry strategy for the client side? we have upstream proxies that will cut off long responses.
[03:45] Carlos: set client timeout to 6s for our medium prompts, retries only on 5xx errors with exponential backoff; avoid retrying on timeouts for long streams to prevent duplicated writes.
[03:56] Samir: A/B versus canary — i worry A/B doubles experiment complexity and user confusion. can we do a canary that also runs golden traffic comparisons without exposing variant to users?
[04:08] Maya: yes, you can do shadow traffic — send duplicates to Redwood and compare outputs offline for quality, then progressively route real traffic. that's a lower user-risk approach.
[04:18] Elena: ok shadowing sounds good for the first 2 phases.
[04:22] Dana: regarding data retention — pilot logs can stay for 30 days, but production will need 90-365 days depending on retention class. we need a plan for PII redaction.
[04:33] Maya: we'll include redaction guidelines and retention configuration options.
[04:38] Josh: for the cutover window, we prefer low-traffic hours — 02:00-04:00 local. is rollback fast? what's the time to revert traffic?
[04:47] Carlos: switching routing is near-instant once you change the policy — actual propagation depends on any edge caches; typical rollback <5 mins for routing, but recovery of cache/warmed state may take longer so your tail latencies can remain elevated for 10-20 mins.
[05:05] Samir: can you define concrete rollback gates? e.g., if p99 > 2s for 15 mins OR error rate > 0.5% for 5 mins we rollback?
[05:16] Maya: that's reasonable. propose formal gates: (1) p99 > 1.5s for 10 mins, (2) error rate > 0.5% for 5 mins, (3) quality metric delta exceeds threshold on evaluation set or human spot checks. if any triggered, immediate rollback and postmortem.
[05:35] Elena: agree, but for the first external canary we want stricter thresholds.
[05:40] Maya: ok tighten for external canary — p99 > 1.2s and error > 0.3%. we'll put both sets in the runbook.
[05:50] Carlos: also add circuit-breaker on the router to fallback to hosted API if dedicated pool is unhealthy; that gives an extra safety net.
[05:59] Dana: will that cause data to leave our VPC? we need to ensure data residency and contractual constraints.
[06:06] Maya: good point — fallback can be configured per-customer. for BrightCart we'll keep fallback within the customer's region; we'll document the dataflow in the security appendix.
[06:17] Priya: i'll coordinate the security appendix with Dana and include the audit log spec.
[06:21] Samir: one more operational ask — who owns the runbook during the pilot? is it Redwood ops or BrightCart SRE?
[06:29] Maya: shared ownership model — Redwood owns the Redwood-side steps and scripts, BrightCart SRE owns traffic policy changes and escalation. we'll include clear ownership in each step.
[06:38] Josh: can you mark the step where we validate warm cache as "manual" for now? our last run had flakiness and we want a human in the loop.
[06:46] Carlos: yes we'll label the warmup validation and provide automated checks as optional.
[06:52] Elena: what's the expected rollback postmortem timeline? we want faster triage.
[06:57] Maya: immediate incident channel, initial triage within 15 minutes, full postmortem within 72 hours. we'll align on severity levels in the runbook.
[07:07] Samir: ok next steps recap?
[07:10] Maya: redwood to share canary runbook + sample k8s manifests by 2026-10-12; carlos to publish benchmark snapshot by 2026-10-11; brightcart to confirm traffic targets and provide SRE on-call details by 2026-10-13; dana to share compliance checklist by 2026-10-14.
[07:33] Elena: yep, sounds good. also please include the shadowing config and how we do offline A/B quality checks.
[07:40] Carlos: will do — we'll include examples and a comparison script.
[07:44] Priya: i'll set up the cutover walkthrough meeting for 2026-10-15 with the SRE team, sending calendar invite after this call.
[07:52] Maya: cool, any final questions?
[07:55] Josh: none from me.
[07:57] Dana: no.
[07:59] Maya: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs.

Transcript notes: occasional mistranscriptions (e.g., "K V cache"), speaker overlaps between Josh and Carlos, some filler words and run-on sentences preserved. References to shared artifacts: runbook link (internal), sample manifests, benchmark spreadsheet (attached separately).

End of call.
